Build and run the current project.

Equivalent to `largo build` followed by executing the resulting binary. The exit code of the built program is propagated.

With `--interpret`, skips the Rust build and runs the program in-process on the bytecode VM, with JIT tier-up on x86-64 Linux and macOS, for fast feedback during development. A concurrent or asynchronous program, or a construct the VM compiler does not take, runs on the tree-walking interpreter instead.

# Example

```bash largo run              # Debug mode (compile to Rust) largo run --release    # Release mode largo run --interpret  # Run in-process on the VM (no Rust build) ```

Usage: largo run [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...

Arguments:
  [ARGS]...
          Arguments to pass to the program

Options:
  -r, --release
          Build with optimizations enabled

  -i, --interpret
          Run in-process on the bytecode VM (JIT where available) instead of building Rust. Gives fast feedback but lacks full compiled-Rust performance

      --emit <EMIT>
          `wasm` compiles straight to a `.wasm` (built-in backend, no rustc) and runs it via the emitted host shim (node). `wasm-linked` links the real `BigInt` runtime first (exact arbitrary-precision integers; needs the Rust toolchain). Compile-and-run in one step

      --engine <ENGINE>
          In-process execution tier. Valid only with `--interpret`

          Possible values:
          - jit:  Optimized bytecode VM with native JIT tier-up
          - vm:   Optimized bytecode VM without native tier-up
          - tree: Optimized tree-walking interpreter

      --max-steps <N>
          Stop after the engine executes N steps (`--interpret` only) — deterministic, the same op on every run. Exhaustion exits 122 with the partial output delivered

      --timeout <DURATION>
          Kill the run after this wall clock (`500ms`, `10s`, `2m`). Expiry exits 124 (the GNU timeout convention)

      --seed <SEED>
          Scheduler seed for deterministic concurrent runs (sets LOGOS_SEED for this run and any compiled child)

      --json
          Print one `logos-run/1` JSON envelope on stdout (`--interpret` only): outcome, output lines, error, steps used

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo run
  largo run --release
  largo run --interpret
  largo run --emit wasm
  largo run -- input.txt --program-flag
